pick.headline: Mob burns the US Embassy in Islamabad
pick.summary: On 21 November 1979 a mob, roused by false reports that the United States was behind the seizure of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, stormed and burned the US Embassy in Islamabad. Four people died, two of them Americans.
pick.significance: Coming weeks after the Tehran embassy seizure, it showed the vulnerability of American diplomats across the region.
pick.fbis: The 21 November 1979 report listed AFP's account of the mob attack on the US Embassy in Islamabad, staff taking refuge in the basement, and Karachi radio reporting that demonstrators had set the embassy on fire.

alternates.headline: Bosnian peace agreement initialled at Dayton
alternates.summary: On 21 November 1995, after three weeks of talks at an Air Force base in Dayton, Ohio, the presidents of Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia initialled a peace agreement.
alternates.significance: The Dayton agreement ended the Bosnian war and committed NATO, including US troops, to enforce it.
alternates.fbis: The East Europe report of 21 November 1995 carried Bosnian radio items from the last days of the Dayton talks, including Bosnian Muslim party support for the Dayton agreement on the Federation.
